title: Writing Expressions with Variables
trouble: Students translate "5 less than n" as 5 − n.

blocks.html: In Grade 5 you wrote expressions from words using only numbers. Now the words can include a variable.
Turn each phrase into an operation, in the order the words describe: "5 more than $n$" is $n + 5$, "5 less than $n$" is $n - 5$, "3 times the sum of $y$ and 4" is $3(y + 4)$.

blocks.name: tapediagram
blocks.cap: "5 less than $n$": start with all of $n$ and take 5 away. What is left is $n - 5$.

blocks.html: Test a phrase with a number. "5 less than 12" is 7, and $12 - 5 = 7$, while $5 - 12$ is not 7. The phrase "5 less than $n$" starts from $n$ and takes 5 away, so $n$ is written first even though 5 is said first. Words like "less than" and "more than" describe a change made to the number that comes after them.

blocks.title: A sum as one quantity
blocks.q: Write "3 times the sum of $y$ and 4".
steps: The sum of $y$ and 4 is $y + 4$, and it is multiplied as a whole, so it goes in parentheses.
$3(y + 4)$. Without parentheses, $3y + 4$ would mean something else.

blocks.title: From a story
blocks.q: Ana had $d$ dollars and spent \$8. Write an expression for the money left.

blocks.html: Writing "5 less than $n$" as $5 - n$, in the order the words are spoken. Quick check: try $n = 12$. Five less than 12 is 7. $12 - 5 = 7$ works; $5 - 12$ does not.
